correctness.rationale: At each ordinary site, an equal adjacent pair is permanently frozen since each endpoint sees its own bit twice. An ordinary path initially alternating cannot keep alternating beyond two updates: odd path endpoints cannot both reverse; even-path parity forces equal neighboring ordinary bits at latest second step. Propagation from a frozen ordinary pair along the finite ordinary path makes every ordinary site eventually constant (or creates further frozen pairs). The distinguished site0 then updates by a constant map if its two ordinary neighbors agree or by complement if they differ, yielding only fixed points or 2-cycles with xor difference precisely site0. In any recurrent state the ordinary path decomposes into maximal constant runs each length≥2; these are sufficient for stability under both hub bits. With q(z)=z²/(1−z), fixed configurations A_n=2[z^{n−1}]q/(1−q²), primitive two-cycles B_n=2[z^{n−1}]q²/(1−q²), giving 2B/(A+2B)→2/3 from the common dominant simple pole (sqrt5−1)/2. Independent exhaustive dynamics over all 2^n initial states for n=3..12 reproduced counts and site0-only two-cycle differences; the frozen-pair proof covers every n≥3.
